To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the maximum power output from the external obliques is higher than previously reported for any muscle and that the power output is maximized by a sawtooth rather than sinusoidal trajectory of length change.

the maximum power outputs of external oblique muscles from two species of tree frogs are similar (54 W kg-1 in Hyla chrysocelis and 58W kg-1 inH. versicolor) and are higher than those of other vertebrate muscles.
the external oblique muscle of the tree frog Hyla chrysocelis has a higher maximum power output and a higher optimum cycle frequency than the muscle of H. versicolor.
